summary.headline: Pyramid Technoplast Q2 FY27 revenue rose 48% YoY to ₹383 crore, EBITDA up 61% to ₹23 crore at 8.5% margin, with capacity utilisation near 70%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a volume-recovery quarter: volumes grew 21% YoY and 14% QoQ to about 14,798 MT, with utilisation at about 70% versus 62% in Q1 FY27. Realisation rose about 22% per ton, driving most of the revenue increase. EBITDA grew 61% YoY to about ₹23 crore, with margin improving to 8.5% from 7.8%. H1 revenue rose 42% to ₹460.5 crore and H1 EBITDA margin was 9%. Management kept FY27 guidance of about 15% revenue growth and 11-12% EBITDA margin, and cut FY27 capex to ₹20-25 crore from about ₹90 crore in FY26. The transcript is poorly transcribed in places, so some figures (notably the revenue unit and some per-kg numbers) are uncertain.

segments.name: Polymer drums
segments.commentary: Tonnage rose 5% YoY and 16% QoQ in Q2; H1 segment revenue about ₹204 crore.

segments.name: IBC (intermediate bulk containers)
segments.commentary: Units grew 17% YoY; value-added IBC is about 32% of Q2 revenue; H1 segment revenue about ₹150-154 crore (figure unclear in transcript).

segments.name: MS drums
segments.commentary: Tonnage grew 73% YoY; H1 segment revenue about ₹64 crore.

segments.name: Recycling plant
segments.commentary: Commissioned October 2025 (investment ₹8-10 crore); contributed about ₹33 lakh EBITDA in Q2 and estimated ~₹2 crore for FY27, payback 2-3 years.

segments.name: Trading income
segments.commentary: Contributed about ₹8.7 crore to the Q2 revenue increase.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: about 15% revenue growth (H1 already up 42%) and EBITDA margin towards 11-12%; management said H1 9% margin plus about 1.5 pts from subsidy and other levers gets there.
Four levers for H2 margin: utilisation, full benefit of captive solar (about ₹15 crore annual savings at full 14.25 MW), recycling plant contribution, and operating leverage/product mix.
Utilisation expected to reach about 80% in FY27 at Vada facility; management also cited 75-80% as a near-term target.
Subsidy: ₹35 crore total approvals (₹24.9 crore Vada over 10 years, ₹10.5 crore Bruch); Vada sanction expected by March 2027, Bruch application in next phase. Benefit to P&L starting March 2027.
FY27 capex planned at ₹20-25 crore (down from about ₹90 crore in FY26), mainly the Cutch expansion; management said the major phase of capacity investment is behind it.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity in Q2 FY27 about 20,993 MT; H1 volume 27,789 MT at about 66% average utilisation.
Cutch facility: about ₹20-25 crore for ~10,000 IBCs per month, expected commissioning by March 2027; to lower freight and improve service in Cutch/Western India.

Solar: 6 MW plus 2.25 MW commissioned October 2025, additional 5 MW at Bruch in February 2026, further 1 MW in next phase; total investment about ₹60 crore; about ₹3.89 crore savings in H1 FY27; management cited about 4-year payback.
Vada facility in full swing across SDP drums, IBCs and MS drums; capacity expansion at Vada would take about 6 months, to start after March.
Management said it would add machines in coming years, sized to actual demand.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is present and volumes are rising month on month; no demand weakness flagged.
Realisation rose about 22% YoY per ton, contributing about ₹43.6 crore of the revenue increase; volume contributed about ₹24.9 crore and trading about ₹8.7 crore.
Over 500 customers; top customer about 6% of revenue, top 10 about 29%.
Management said raw-material cost is passed through to customers; gross profit per kg steady-state cited around ₹33-35 (analyst-reported, unclear).
Management said the Vada and IBC business is being sold into chemical customers; pharma and food-grade approvals exist but are not a major focus.

qa_highlights.question: How will H1 margin of about 9% bridge to the 11-12% FY27 target, and what contribution is expected from subsidy, solar and recycling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin should reach about 9% for FY27 with subsidy adding roughly 1.5 pts; recycling demand is rising and capacity is being added. Bridge details were not quantified clearly in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sharply, and is EBITDA per ton or margin the right metric?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to higher transport costs (long-route customers, Cutch expansion to reduce freight) and employee costs as staff returned from leave. Management said to focus on EBITDA per ton, which it said is constant and will improve.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 70% utilisation below the FY27 target of 80%, and is the FY27 guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said demand is present and volumes are increasing, targeting 75-80% utilisation; it said guidance is being set to be exceeded, without quantifying a higher number.

qa_highlights.question: Why was cash flow negative in H1, and how will it accumulate by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the negative flow is from higher debtors and working capital tied up in the growing business, and that it is not structurally negative. Analyst pushed for detail on interest and borrowing schedule; management deferred to an offline follow-up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for solar benefits and the recycling plant contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Solar about 89% of expected savings realised so far, with remaining installation hopefully producing benefit next month. Recycling expected to add about ₹2 crore FY27 and ₹4-5 crore next year.

risks_watch: Rising transport and other expenses; management described a per-kg increase (₹17 to ₹19 per kg referenced) and said logistics costs will ease with Cutch capacity.
Negative H1 cash flow and rising debtors; finance cost up 147% YoY, so debt and interest schedule needs watching.
Subsidy recognition (Vada sanction by March 2027) and Bruch sanction timing are not yet confirmed.
Utilisation at ~70% against a stated 80% FY27 target; watch Q3 utilisation step-up.
Transcript quality is poor: several figures (revenue unit, segment revenue, per-kg numbers, cash flow amounts) are uncertain and should be verified against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on volumes, utilisation and the margin trajectory, but became evasive and disorganised under questioning on transport costs, cash flow and per-kg metrics, often deferring detail to offline follow-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Cutch IBC facility (~10,000 IBCs/month, ₹20-25 cr) is under construction with commissioning expected by March 2027, and Vada expansion (~6 months build) starts after March 2027; installed capacity is about 20,993 MT against 14,798 MT Q2 volume.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume rose 21% YoY and 14% QoQ to 14,798 MT, utilisation rose from 62% to ~70%, and management targets 75-80% near term and about 80% in FY27.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is cut to ₹20-25 cr from ~₹90 cr and management says the major capacity phase is behind it, though it will add machines sized to demand and utilisation at ~70% is below the 80% target.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue is already up 42% against about 15% FY27 guidance, and management said guidance is set to be exceeded, but it did not quantify a higher number.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Transport and employee costs rose sharply, finance cost is up 147% YoY, H1 cash flow was negative, and subsidy sanction for Vada (₹24.9 cr) is not yet confirmed until March 2027.

rows.label: Captive solar savings and recycling plant contribution
rows.why: Solar is about 89% of expected savings realised, with about ₹3.89 cr saved in H1 FY27, and recycling is expected to add about ₹2 cr in FY27 and ₹4-5 cr next year.

rows.label: Vada subsidy sanction (₹24.9 cr over 10 years)
rows.why: Sanction is expected by March 2027 with P&L benefit starting then, but Bruch's ₹10.5 cr application is only in the next phase and not confirmed.

rows.label: Negative H1 cash flow reversal
rows.why: Management said the negative flow comes from higher debtors and working capital and is not structurally negative, but gave no quantified accumulation schedule and deferred the borrowing detail offline.
